translationRepairs: yiyin became a cook, Baili Xi became a captive—all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.
Yi Yin became a cook, Baili Xi became a captive—all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.
伊尹 is the personal name Yi Yin; the fused lowercase "yiyin" is a real error, and the proposed capitalization/spacing is accurate without other change.
yiyin became cook, Baili Xi became captive, all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.
Yi Yin became cook, Baili Xi became captive, all the paths by which they petitioned their superiors.
The literal field likewise fails to render 伊尹 as the name Yi Yin; correcting "yiyin" to "Yi Yin" matches the Chinese without semantic invention.
In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus he married his son to them.
In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus he married his daughter to their ruler.

以其子妻之 uses 妻 as a verb 'to give as wife,' so 子 here is a daughter given in marriage to Hu's side; "married his son" reverses the marital relation, and the proposed daughter-to-ruler wording restores it.
In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus married his son to them.
In ancient times Zheng Wu Gong wished to attack Hu, thus married his daughter to them.
The literal likewise misreads 妻之 as marrying a son; replacing "son" with "daughter" correctly reflects giving the child as a wife to Hu.
Therefore, these two sons, all sages, yet could not avoid debasing their persons and entering the world in such filth, then this is not what able service establishes.
Therefore, these two men, both sages, yet could not avoid debasing their persons and entering the world in such filth; then this is not what those able to serve establish.
二子者 refers to Yi Yin and Baili Xi as two gentlemen, not sons; 皆 with two people is "both," and 非能仕之所設也 is better rendered as what those able to serve establish than "able service establishes."
